prerequisites: Estructuras Discretas y Análisis de Algoritmos

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the state-space search paradigm and know how to use it to solve combinatorial optimization problems. Know how to model search spaces for specific problems and how to incorporate problem domain knowledge into algorithms to improve their efficiency.

Understand Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) and Optimization (CSOPs). Know how to formulate these types of problems and how to solve them using search and inference techniques (constraint propagation).
Understand metaheuristics and know how to use them to solve combinatorial and numerical optimization problems, with one or more objective functions.
Know how to apply the above methods to problems specific to data science and engineering, such as decision tree calculation, clustering methods, neural network training, etc.

syllabus_topics: Trajectory-based metaheuristics. Local search and simulated annealing
Classification. Lexicographical optimization and Pareto optimization
teaching_methods: Asynchronous online training activities (videos, recommended readings, solved examples)

assessment_methods.method: Partial exam (T1) on contents of Theme 1 and Theme 2
Partial exam (T2) on contents of Theme 3 and Theme 4

assessment_rules: To pass in the ordinary call, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in both the theoretical and practical blocks. The final theoretical grade is (T1 x 0.5) + (T2 x 0.5), and the final practical grade is (P1 x 0.25) + (P2 x 0.25) + (P3 x 0.5). If minimums are met, the final grade is (Theoretical grade x 0.45) + (Practical grade x 0.4) + (Attendance x 0.05) + (Active Participation x 0.1); otherwise, the grade is the minimum of this formula and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, theoretical and practical parts are evaluated similarly, and final grades for each element are the maximum of the ordinary and extraordinary call scores. If minimums are met, the final grade is (TE1 x 0.5 + TE2 x 0.5) x 0.53 + (PE1 x 0.25 + PE2 x 0.25 + PE3 x 0.5) x 0.47; otherwise, the grade is the minimum of this formula and 4.0.
